name: Out-of-core Interval Tree Extraction
definition: A method for isosurface extraction where the interval tree and associated min/max lists are stored on disk in blocks, and only necessary blocks are loaded based on isovalue intervals.
summary: Out-of-core Interval Tree Extraction enables isosurface extraction for datasets larger than main memory by storing the interval tree on disk and explicitly modeling I/O cost based on isovalue probability distributions.
